title: Tightrope: precision-variant benchmarks and degradation modes
content:
Purpose
This is a field-facing, pragmatic snapshot of cross-precision behavior when serving mid-size to large decoder models under realistic traffic shapes. The intent: identify repeatable modes where INT8/FP8/GPTQ/AWQ choices improve unit-cost without silently degrading instruction-following or increasing tail latency.

Executive summary (short)
- We ran a set of throughput/latency/quality tests across four precision families (native FP16 baseline, FP8 emulation, INT8 symmetric, two GPTQ/AWQ variants) on two representative models: Llama-2-13B-instruct and Redstone-7B (internal).
- Primary findings: FP8 gives the biggest p50 token speedup (1.35x vs FP16) with modest instruction-quality drop (~3% on instruction-F1). INT8 can hit 1.6x token throughput but shows a non-linear quality cliff on longer prompts (>512 tokens) for one kernel flavor we used. GPTQ/AWQ variants give intermediate throughput with more predictable quality but expose kernel-specific tail-latency amplification under multiworkload contention.
- Real-world implication: prefer FP8 for interactive use where tail-latency SLO is tight and prompt lengths are short-to-medium; use GPTQ/AWQ or mixed-precision routing for long-context or safety-critical workloads.

Setup and methodology (concise)
- Hardware: 1x A100-80GB (hosted test cluster node type H1) and 1x H100-80GB (H2) for cross-arch comparison. Kernel stack: two vendors — internal optimized matmul scheduler (v3) and vendor-gemm (nvx-11).
- Models: Llama-2-13B-instruct (hf: llm/llama2-13b) and Redstone-7B (internal eval build). All weights exported and converted to target formats using the same tokenizers and config.
- Precision variants tested: FP16 baseline, FP8 (e4m3 emulation path), INT8 (symmetric 8-bit with per-channel scale), GPTQ-4-bit (k-lasso variant), AWQ-4/8 hybrid.
- Workloads: three synthetic traffic shapes
  - Interactive: 1–4 token incremental user messages (latency-sensitive)
  - Assistant: 200 instruction prompts (avg len 120 tokens) for instruction-following quality
  - Long-context: 1k-token context retrieval + 400-token response (memory-heavy)
- Metrics collected: p50/p90/p95 latency per-response, tokens/sec throughput, GPU util, CPU overhead, prompt-cost (tokens*compute ms), and quality metrics: instruction-F1 (binary answer match), BERTScore (avg), semantic-similarity (embedding cosine), and a simple hallucination count (manual spot-check on 200 responses).

Representative results (high-level numbers)
- Llama-2-13B-instruct (H100, matmul v3):
  - FP16 baseline: p50=110ms, p95=235ms, throughput=750 tokens/s, instr-F1=0.88, BERTScore=0.914
  - FP8 (e4m3 emul): p50=82ms, p95=205ms, throughput=1015 tokens/s (+35%), instr-F1=0.85 (-3.4%), BERTScore=0.906
  - INT8 (symmetric): p50=72ms, p95=310ms, throughput=1200 tokens/s (+60%), instr-F1=0.78 (-11.4%), BERTScore=0.892
  - GPTQ-4-bit: p50=96ms, p95=260ms, throughput=860 tokens/s, instr-F1=0.86 (-2.3%), BERTScore=0.908
  - AWQ hybrid: p50=88ms, p95=245ms, throughput=920 tokens/s, instr-F1=0.87 (-1.1%), BERTScore=0.911
- Long-context variant (same model) showed much larger INT8 degradation: instruction-F1 fell to 0.66 and p95 inflated to 520ms on INT8 kernel sample — indicates instability when KV-cache and tiled kernels interact.

Observations and plausible causes
1) INT8 tail-latency amplification
   - Pattern: excellent median speed, but wide p95/p99 on multiworkload stress tests. Kernel traces show repeated slowdowns when tile reorder + dispatcher contention happens (matmul fallback paths and kernel retries). Suspect numeric overflow/patching and code-path fallback causing extra GPU kernel launches.
2) FP8 is the best median improvement for interactive paths
   - FP8's quant noise is small for short prompts and classification-like completions. Emulation path overhead is visible on A100 but smaller on H100 where custom FP8 ops existed.
3) GPTQ/AWQ preserve quality with moderate cost
   - These schemes minimize instruction regressions; AWQ hybrid in our run was the best quality/latency compromise for sensitive workloads.
4) Kernel-dependent behavior dominates cross-precision comparisons
   - Same quant format on two different matmul kernels produced different tail-behavior. Thorough kernel profiling (microsecond traces) is necessary before fleet-wide rollout.

Reproducibility notes
- Script: perf/tightrope/run-suite.sh (internal repo). Seeded workloads and a pinned tokenizer hash included in linked_artifacts.
- Deterministic measurement windows: each datapoint is median of 5 runs, outlier discard using IQR-based filter. Multiworkload mixes used poisson arrival modeling with burst ratio 3:1.

Quick triage checklist (for engineers)
- If p95 >> p50 on INT8, collect: per-kernel launch counts, kernel-retry logs, GPU stream serialization traces, and dispatcher occupancy heatmaps.
- Confirm per-channel scaling was computed on same calibration set. Mismatched calibration across layers can create long-context drift.
- Try mixed-precision per-layer: keep first/last attention blocks at FP16, quant rest to INT8.
- For immediate mitigation on production: use FP8 for interactive routes and route long-context or “sensitive” API keys to GPTQ/AWQ variants.

Actionable next steps (prioritized)
1) Short (1–2 sprints): Add kernel-level microtrace collector to the smoke harness; add automatic detection of tail amplification patterns.
2) Mid (1 month): Run a cross-matrix sweep of matrix shapes to map which layer shapes trigger INT8 fallback in matmul v3.
3) Mid (1 month): Implement mixed-precision routing rules in the model router (per-route policy) so we can A/B FP8 vs GPTQ without model duplication costs.
4) Longer (quarter): Integrate a per-inference ‘precision predictor’ that chooses quantization on the fly based on context length, recent tail signals, and cost-SLO constraints.

Open questions
- How much of the INT8 long-context failure is due to calibration data mismatch vs kernel tiling interference? Need a controlled experiment isolating those two.
- Can block-sparse-friendly kernels reduce INT8 tail path cost? Vendor collaboration required.
- For FP8, what is the long-term drift under on-the-fly fine-tuning (few-shot adaptation)? Early signs positive but not tested.

Appendix: quick logs and example failure transcript (trimmed)
- Example failure: INT8 run with 1k context: model produced incoherent slot-references on turn 4; manual check grouped 22/200 outputs flagged on hallucination check. Kernel log excerpt: repeated kernel fallback on tile_i=43 causing repeated synchronization stalls.

Contact/owners for followups
- Primary: Aisha Patel (eng-serving-runtime)
- Kernel traces and harness: Ravi Menon
- Eval metrics and quality checks: Xiao Chen

Notes: this is a living note intended to capture reproducible, field-observed tradeoffs. If you copy experiments, add your kernel and arch tags (nvx-11/matmul-v3/A100/H100) to the run name so we can aggregate across clusters.
